A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 40-page paper, including readable equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–B. Their content can be matched reliably throughout.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM transmission-chain experiments measuring toxicity, positivity, difficulty and length, with robustness checks and empirical validation in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experimental results, including the six-model comparisons, attractor estimates and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same iterative transmission procedure, prompting tasks, property measurements and regression-based attractor estimator.

E1.justification: Both use the same scientific abstracts, news articles and social-media comments for Rephrase, Take inspiration and Continue. The additional task variants and heterogeneous-chain scenarios in Appendix B are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The six-model comparison retains the same participants, including GPT-4o-mini in both versions. The Base/Instruct comparisons in Figure 5b and homogeneous/heterogeneous comparisons in Figure S6 also match.

E3.justification: Both retain 50-step chains, 20 initial texts in the main experiment, the same four property metrics, generation settings and output preprocessing. The appendix experiments use unchanged protocols.

E4.justification: The temperature and fine-tuning analyses, sample-size and prompt-phrasing robustness checks, task-constraint controls, heterogeneous chains, collapse case study and attractor validation are all retained unchanged (Figure 5; Appendix B).

E5.justification: Both report five seeds, the same standard-error and standard-deviation displays, KS tests and Bayesian 95% credible intervals. Appendix B retains the same statistical procedures and uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Corresponding Figures 2–5 and S2–S28 and Tables 1–13 contain the same plotted results, numerical entries and generated-text examples. No reported estimate, trend, ranking or qualitative finding changes.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 preserves the linear recurrence, convergence condition |s| < 1, attractor position I/(1-s) and strength 1-s. The statistical model definitions in Appendix B.3 are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain the same claims about single-turn evaluation gaps, cultural-attractor measures and how transmission dynamics depend on models, tasks and text properties.

C2.justification: The interpretations of temperature, fine-tuning, task constraints and collapse are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations and proposed extensions beyond linear chains to networks and human–LLM interactions.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same prompts, sampling and filtering instructions, hyperparameters, precision and computational-resource disclosures. The reproducibility statement provides unchanged code and data access information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged, including positioning relative to cultural attraction theory, Bayesian iterated learning and earlier artificial-agent transmission studies.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 2 June 2025 to v4 dated 29 January 2026, with its version-specific link updated. The title, authors, scientific text and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5, Figures S1–S28 and Tables 1–13 retain their graphics, captions, labels and placement. The main-paper and appendix layouts are preserved; negligible glyph-position shifts do not alter the displays.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, experimental evidence, theoretical reasoning, limitations and reproducibility information are unchanged throughout both PDFs, including the appendices. Updating the arXiv stamp and its link produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
